t.7.91.1: Hearing that Bharata had arrived as commander of the army, accompanied by Gārgya, Yudhājit, lord of the Kekayas, attained supreme joy.
t.7.91.2: The lord of the Kekayas set forth with a great multitude of people, and, hastening, he advanced against the Gandharvas, who were godlike in form.
t.7.91.3: Bharata and Yudhājit, united together and swift in their stride, reached the city of the Gandharvas along with their army and their followers.
t.7.91.4: Hearing that Bharata had arrived, those Gandharvas, of great valour and eager to fight, assembled together, roaring on every side.
t.7.91.5: Then there arose a tumultuous battle, hair-raising and exceedingly terrible, lasting seven nights, and victory went to neither of the two.
t.7.91.6: Then Bharata, the younger brother of Rāma, enraged, loosed upon the Gandharvas the most dreadful weapon of Kāla, named Saṃvarta.
t.7.91.7: Bound by the noose of Time and torn apart by the Saṃvarta, three crores of them were struck down there in an instant by the great-souled one.
t.7.91.8: The dwellers of heaven do not remember so terrible a slaughter of such great-souled beings, accomplished in the mere space of the twinkling of an eye.
t.7.91.9: When those heroes had been slain, Bharata, the son of Kaikayī, then established two prosperous and excellent cities, settling Takṣa in Takṣaśilā and Puṣkara in Puṣkarāvatī.
t.7.91.10: Within five years, that lovely land of the Gandharvas, the Gāndhāra country, came to be filled with provinces and with townsfolk as well.
t.7.91.11: The two cities were filled with masses of wealth and jewels and adorned with groves; built as if in rivalry with one another, they vied in the abundance of their excellences.
t.7.91.13: Both those excellent and delightful cities were adorned with broad expanses, with splendid chief mansions, and with very beautiful palaces of uniform colour.
t.7.91.12: Both cities were most splendid in appearance, marked by honest dealings, filled with gardens and throngs of vehicles, and furnished with well-laid-out markets.
t.7.91.15: Glorious Bharata saluted the great-souled Rāghava, who was like a second Dharma in visible form, just as Vāsava salutes Brahmā.
t.7.91.14: When the two cities had been adorned with splendid and spacious temples, Bharata, the mighty-armed younger brother of Rāghava and son of Kaikayī, having settled them over five years, returned once more to Ayodhyā.
t.7.91.16: And he recounted, just as it had happened, the splendid slaying of the Gandharvas and the settling of the land; hearing this from him, Rāghava was delighted.
